name: Valid minimal request, no origin header, host localhost without port → 200
spec_quote: The origin header must be absent, the literal "null", or "http://localhost" / "http://127.0.0.1" optionally with ":port" ... Otherwise → [200, {"id": id, "pref": pref}].

name: Path with query string, host and origin with port, content-type with charset → 200
spec_quote: The path without its query string must be exactly "/pref" ... parameters like "; charset=utf-8" are fine ... Otherwise → [200, {"id": id, "pref": pref}].

name: Host check wins over path and method: bad host with GET /prefs → 421
spec_quote: Checks, in this order (the first that fails decides the answer) ... The host header must be "localhost" or "127.0.0.1", optionally followed by ":" and a port of 1–5 digits (anything else, or no host header) → 421 "bad host"

name: No host header at all → 421 bad host
spec_quote: (anything else, or no host header) → 421 "bad host"

name: Host port with 6 digits → 421 bad host
spec_quote: optionally followed by ":" and a port of 1–5 digits (anything else, or no host header) → 421 "bad host"

name: Trailing slash path /pref/ → 404 unknown path
spec_quote: The path without its query string must be exactly "/pref" → 404 "unknown path"

name: Path check runs before method: GET on /other → 404 not 405
spec_quote: Checks, in this order (the first that fails decides the answer) ... 2. The path without its query string must be exactly "/pref" → 404 "unknown path" 3. The method must be "POST" → 405 "POST only"

name: GET on /pref → 405 POST only
spec_quote: The method must be "POST" → 405 "POST only"

name: https origin → 403 origin not allowed
spec_quote: the literal "null", or "http://localhost" / "http://127.0.0.1" optionally with ":port" (1–5 digits) and nothing else (no path, no https, no other host) → 403 "origin not allowed"

name: Origin with extra path → 403 origin not allowed
spec_quote: optionally with ":port" (1–5 digits) and nothing else (no path, no https, no other host) → 403 "origin not allowed"

name: Literal "null" origin is allowed → 200
spec_quote: The origin header must be absent, the literal "null", or "http://localhost" / "http://127.0.0.1" ... Otherwise → [200, {"id": id, "pref": pref}].

name: Missing x-jsa-pref header → 403 missing X-JSA-Pref header
spec_quote: The x-jsa-pref header must be exactly "1" → 403 "missing X-JSA-Pref header"

name: x-jsa-pref value "true" is not exactly "1" → 403
spec_quote: The x-jsa-pref header must be exactly "1" → 403 "missing X-JSA-Pref header"

name: Missing content-type header → 415
spec_quote: The content-type header must start with "application/json" (case-insensitive; parameters like "; charset=utf-8" are fine) → 415 "Content-Type must be application/json"

name: Upper-case content-type with parameter → 200 (case-insensitive)
spec_quote: The content-type header must start with "application/json" (case-insensitive; parameters like "; charset=utf-8" are fine) ... Otherwise → [200, {"id": id, "pref": pref}].

name: Body of 1025 bytes (valid JSON padded with spaces) → 413 body too large
spec_quote: The body must be at most 1024 bytes → 413 "body too large"

name: Content-type check precedes size check: text/plain with oversized body → 415
spec_quote: Checks, in this order (the first that fails decides the answer) ... 6. The content-type header must start with "application/json" ... → 415 ... 7. The body must be at most 1024 bytes → 413

name: Non-JSON body → 400 body is not JSON
spec_quote: The body must parse as JSON → 400 "body is not JSON"

name: JSON array body (not an object) → 400 body must be a JSON object {id, pref}

expect.error: body must be a JSON object {id, pref}

spec_quote: It must be a JSON object whose keys are exactly "id" and "pref" (no more, no fewer) → 400 "body must be a JSON object {id, pref}"

name: Object with an extra key → 400 body must be a JSON object {id, pref}

expect.error: body must be a JSON object {id, pref}

spec_quote: It must be a JSON object whose keys are exactly "id" and "pref" (no more, no fewer) → 400 "body must be a JSON object {id, pref}"

name: id with only 3 digits → 400 bad id
spec_quote: id must be a string: "J" followed by 4 to 6 digits, nothing else → 400 "bad id"

name: pref "UP" (wrong case) → 400 pref must be up, down or clear

expect.error: pref must be up, down or clear

spec_quote: pref must be one of "up", "down", "clear" (exact, lower case) → 400 "pref must be up, down or clear"

name: Apply up to a single id without prior preference
spec_quote: pref "up" sets joey_pref = "up" and joey_pref_on = today's date (YYYY-MM-DD) on each id ... one log line per id is appended

name: Apply down to two ids, one of which was already up
spec_quote: "down" likewise with "down" ... one log line per id is appended

name: Apply clear to a row that had a preference
spec_quote: "clear" removes both fields (a row without them stays without them) ... one log line per id is appended

name: Apply clear to a row that had no preference: unchanged, still one log line
spec_quote: "clear" removes both fields (a row without them stays without them) ... one log line per id is appended

name: One unknown id in the list: nothing written, no log lines
spec_quote: If any id is not in the table, nothing is written (table and log unchanged) and the unknown ids are reported.

name: Only the listed id changes; other rows keep their preferences
spec_quote: Rows other than the given ids are not changed by the preference. ... one log line per id is appended

name: Unknown id (J88888) among otherwise valid ids: no writes at all
spec_quote: If any id is not in the table, nothing is written (table and log unchanged) and the unknown ids are reported.

name: Apply up to three ids in a four-row table: three log lines, fourth row untouched
spec_quote: "up" sets joey_pref = "up" ... on each id ... Rows other than the given ids are not changed by the preference. ... one log line per id is appended
